paragraphs: Dream Jobs, by May. On Thursday, the Explorers had a meeting in the school library. Teacher Kim showed us the news on a big screen. In the video, a rocket went up into space. The rocket was white and very loud, and all the children were quiet. Then I asked the children, "Which job do you want?" Here are their dream jobs.

The Astronaut. An astronaut travels in a rocket to space. In space, the astronaut lives in a small room. She or he stays there for many days. An astronaut must be strong and must learn for many years. Leo wants to be an astronaut. "I like to look at the planet from far away," he said.

The Pilot and the Engineer. A pilot flies a plane. Pilots all over the world talk to each other in English. Some pilots fly small planes, and some fly big planes with many people. I want to be a pilot, because English is my favorite lesson. An engineer builds big things, like a rocket or a bridge. Mia wants to be an engineer. She loves animals, so her dream is about them. "I want to build a safe road for animals," she said. Lily has not decided yet, because she likes many jobs.

A Job for Leo. Then Leo said, "A restaurant in space needs a waiter, too!" A waiter brings food to the table on a plate. He or she walks slowly and does not drop anything. Leo carried two plates across the library and did not drop them. "Here is your space food, Teacher Kim," he said. Teacher Kim laughed and took a plate. Then all the children clapped for the waiter.
"Every job is important," said Teacher Kim. "Today you have a dream, and one day you will do it." Which dream job do you like? Tell us in a message under this page!
text.summary: After a news video about a rocket, May writes a page for Explorers' Blog about dream jobs. She tells what an astronaut, a pilot, and an engineer do, and Leo makes the class laugh with a job in a space restaurant.
